findings.recoveredFrom: 20-core.md 'Not checked' section, lines 253-261 (a reproduced delegate medium that was never given a finding number)
findings.title: an aggressive panorama-band crop re-rasterizes scaled strokes at the original brush radius, growing unpainted columns until a Blocked target reads as Observable
findings.impact: cropping a panorama to a narrower band scales the existing strokes but keeps the original brush radius, so widening the visible azimuth per pixel leaves gaps in the painted band. Measured at the default brush r=28: 11 of 91 in-frame bins lost, and a column that was {"code":"blk","text":"Blocked"} (ceil 37.10) becomes {"code":"vis","text":"Observable"} (ceil -90). A target the user marked as blocked by an obstacle is then planned as observable - the same class of silent safety inversion the panorama editor exists to prevent.
findings.mechanism: `cropStrokes` transforms stroke geometry into the new frame but does not scale the brush radius with the horizontal scale factor, so the stroke mask no longer covers the band it covered before the crop.
findings.evidence: `node reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/core/probe_moneyshot.mjs` -> `lost 11 of 91 in-frame bins; first hole az 52 / alt 30 BEFORE {"code":"blk","text":"Blocked"} ceil 37.10 / AFTER {"code":"vis","text":"Observable"} ceil -90`.
findings.repro: `node reviews/0.6.32-full/evidence/core/probe_moneyshot.mjs` (reachable while `p.strokes` is non-empty).
findings.requiredFix: scale the rasterization brush radius by the same horizontal factor applied to the stroke geometry in `cropStrokes`, then re-derive the profile - or refuse a crop that would thin the painted band below the brush pitch.
findings.counterArgument: a real pointer drag paints densely enough that a user may never produce the gap, and the lane did not build the end-to-end browser scenario with a realistic pitch, so the practical frequency is unmeasured. The mechanism and the Blocked -> Observable transition are both reproduced, which is what makes this a finding rather than a suspicion.

findings.recoveredFrom: 20-core.md lines 177-195 (the 'Scoring/catalogue delegate digest', prose rather than a numbered finding)
findings.title: type lookups use plain object literals, so a crafted `otype` of `"toString"` reaches `Object.prototype` and defeats the fallback
findings.impact: a setup bundle carrying `otype: "toString"` survives the import (`app/database.py:986` stores it verbatim) and every `X[t] || fallback` returns an inherited `Object.prototype` member instead of falling back: the type cell renders native function source and the moon-aware score becomes `NaN`.
findings.mechanism: `TYPE_LABELS`, `TYPE_COLORS` and `MOON_TYPE_FACTOR` are object literals, so a key that collides with `Object.prototype` is truthy before the `||` fallback is reached.
findings.evidence: `core/catalog.js:10-25`, `core/scoring.js:15-19,29`, `static/js/skymap.js:204`; `app/database.py:986` stores `otype` verbatim.
findings.repro: import a bundle whose custom/panorama record carries `otype: "toString"`, then open the object's type cell and enable moon-aware ranking.
findings.requiredFix: `Object.assign(Object.create(null), {...})` for the three maps (or `Object.hasOwn` before the lookup) plus a `|| "unknown"` at `static/js/skymap.js:204`.
findings.counterArgument: every in-app producer clamps `otype`, so the worst case is garbled text plus a ranking key that is never rendered; the lane notes the calibration should rise if setup bundles are treated as untrusted, which this review does treat them as.

findings.recoveredFrom: 20-core.md lines 205-208, a cross-lane note the web lane never filed; verified by the captain at the cited lines
findings.title: the web sky chart excludes no-magnitude ADVANCED rows at every slider position, contradicting the shared magnitude rule
findings.impact: `base.filter((o) => o._adv && o.vmag != null && magVisible(...))` drops every advanced object without a measured magnitude unconditionally, so those objects never reach the Sky View chart - not even with the magnitude slider at its maximum, where the documented rule says they should appear. The 9 batch-2 supplement objects (0.6.29) deliberately ship `vmag` empty and are advanced-mode-only, so the newest additions cannot be plotted; the Targets list still shows them, which is the workaround.
findings.mechanism: the standard branch at `:869` uses only `magVisible(o.vmag, S.skyMag, magMax)` (which admits no-magnitude rows at the maximum), while the advanced branch at `:870` adds an explicit `o.vmag != null` guard before it - the extra guard is what breaks parity.
findings.evidence: `web/app.js:868-872` read by the captain; the comment at `:865-867` states "Objects with no measured magnitude show only at the slider maximum", and `AGENTS.md` pins the rule as filtering EVERY object. No test covers the advanced branch (the `mag` engine tests the shared helper, not this call site).
findings.repro: open the web planner in advanced mode, set the target list's magnitude/visibility controls to maximum, and look for a `vmag`-empty object (e.g. `sh2-240`) on the Sky View chart - it is in the Targets table but absent from the chart. Static reading of `:868-872` is sufficient to confirm; the browser run was not repeated for this item.
findings.requiredFix: drop the extra `o.vmag != null` guard so the advanced branch uses the same `magVisible(o.vmag, S.skyMag, magMax)` call as the standard branch (the 1400-object brightness cap can stay).
findings.counterArgument: the guard may be a deliberate responsiveness bound for the advanced pool, and the comment's "additionally capped at 1400 by brightness" shows intent to restrict that branch - but the cap alone would not require excluding no-magnitude rows, and nothing in `AGENTS.md` or a test declares this exception, so it is an undocumented divergence rather than a stated policy.

findings.recoveredFrom: captain's gate run (filed by the captain; no lane ran the gate)
findings.title: the desktop pano-crop browser check still times out on a cold first launch, even after the post-tag 30 s -> 90 s wait fix
findings.file: `tests/browser/desktop_suite.py` (the crop check's upload wait); post-tag commit d6ace7a 'browser gate: the desktop crop check's upload wait is flaky at 30 s'
findings.impact: `python scripts/check_browser.py --all` reports 21/22 with `desktop-pano-crop-fov` failing at 91.9 s, while an immediate re-run of the same check passes in 3.0 s. Whoever runs the documented release checklist on a cold machine gets a red gate and must know the re-run rule to tell a flake from a regression - which is exactly what a release gate exists to remove.
findings.mechanism: the PyInstaller onefile exe unpacks into %TEMP% on first launch; after the 14 web checks have just run, that first desktop launch exceeds the check's 90 s `wait_for_function`. Raising the wait from 30 s (d6ace7a) moved the threshold without removing the cold-start dependency, and the cold path is now measured at ~92 s - above the new limit.

findings.title: the panorama editor legend promises a green alt-0 horizon guide that is not drawn, and keys none of the painted state
findings.file: the legend text rendered by `web/horizon.js` vs the canvas drawn via `core/horizon.js`
findings.impact: the legend reads 'Guides: amber = azimuth (N/E/S/W), green dashed = horizon (alt 0), blue = altitude', but no green pixels exist on the canvas in either theme or width; the alt-0 position coincides with the plot's bottom border in the same blue as the frame, so the horizon line is indistinguishable from the frame.
